statement.p:
Suppose that A is the 4\times3 matrix whose columns are
\vvec_1 = \fourvec1111,\hspace{24pt} \vvec_2 = \fourvec1322,\hspace{24pt} \vvec_3 = \fourvec1{-3}{-3}{-3}\text{.}
These vectors form a basis for W, the subspace of \real^4 that we encountered in . Since these vectors are the columns of A, we have \col(A) = W.
When we implemented Gram-Schmidt, we first found an orthogonal basis \wvec_1, \wvec_2, and \wvec_3 using
\begin{aligned} \wvec_1 \amp = \vvec_1 \\ \wvec_2 \amp = \vvec_2 - \frac{\vvec_2\cdot\wvec_1}{\wvec_1\cdot\wvec_1}\wvec_1 \\ \wvec_3 \amp = \vvec_3 - \frac{\vvec_3\cdot\wvec_1}{\wvec_1\cdot\wvec_1}\wvec_1 - \frac{\vvec_3\cdot\wvec_2}{\wvec_2\cdot\wvec_2}\wvec_2\text{.} \\ \end{aligned}
Use these expressions to write \vvec_1, \vvec_2, and \vvec_3 as linear combinations of \wvec_1, \wvec_2, and \wvec_3.
We next normalized the orthogonal basis \wvec_1, \wvec_2, and \wvec_3 to obtain an orthonormal basis \uvec_1, \uvec_2, and \uvec_3.
Write the vectors \wvec_i as scalar multiples of \uvec_i. Then use these expressions to write \vvec_1, \vvec_2, and \vvec_3 as linear combinations of \uvec_1, \uvec_2, and \uvec_3.
Suppose that Q = \left[ \begin{array}{ccc} \uvec_1 \amp \uvec_2 \amp \uvec_3 \end{array} \right]. Use the result of the previous part to find a vector \rvec_1 so that Q\rvec_1 = \vvec_1.
Then find vectors \rvec_2 and \rvec_3 such that Q\rvec_2 = \vvec_2 and Q\rvec_3 = \vvec_3.
Construct the matrix R = \left[ \begin{array}{ccc} \rvec_1 \amp \rvec_2 \amp \rvec_3 \end{array} \right]. Remembering that A = \left[ \begin{array}{ccc} \vvec_1 \amp \vvec_2 \amp \vvec_3 \end{array} \right], explain why A = QR.
What is special about the shape of R?
Suppose that A is a 10\times 6 matrix whose columns are linearly independent. This means that the columns of A form a basis for W=\col(A), a 6-dimensional subspace of \real^{10}. Suppose that we apply Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization to create an orthonormal basis whose vectors form the columns of Q and that we write A=QR. What are the shape of Q and what the shape of R?

li.p: In the same way, we have \vvec_2 = Q\threevec4{\sqrt{2}}0 and \vvec_3=Q\threevec{-4}{-2\sqrt{2}}2.
We have QR = \begin{bmatrix} Q\rvec_1 \amp Q\rvec_2 \amp Q\rvec_3 \end{bmatrix} = A.
Q will be 10\times6 and R will be a 6\times 6 upper triangular matrix.
We have QR = \begin{bmatrix} Q\rvec_1 \amp Q\rvec_2 \amp Q\rvec_3 \end{bmatrix} = A.
Q will be 10\times6 and R will be 6\times 6.
